summary: 32-phase plan for discharging the CS5 pair-seed obligation. Stage A repairs the refutable statement, collapses three obligations to one, and discharges the new side condition at the caller. Stages B-F formalise a cut-free nested-sequent system for CS5 (Arisaka-Das-Strassburger safe pair X={t,4}, Y={b}). Stage G extends it to the two-label CS5Pair signature. Estimated 86 hours.
decisions_made: Primary route is cut-free nested sequents, not the product model: the product route's residual R-b instantiated at H := cl_CS5(empty) yields IS5 subset CS5, i.e. the CS5=IS5 collapse the mandate has not adopted. Phase 5 machine-checks this reduction.
Cut-elimination alone is not sufficient; the two-label bridge (Stage G) is planned explicitly and flagged as the larger risk, with Phase 28 (cross-rule permutation) named as the crux.
Cross rules are designed via axioms-as-rules (Negri) rather than fed by cut, to maximise the chance Phase 28 succeeds.
In-repo LJ/CutElimination.lean (711 lines, sorry-free) is the architectural template for Stage F; contexts use Observation 2.2 normal form so well-formedness is definitional.
Landed cs5Pair_derivExcludes_of_disjunctionProperty is left textually unchanged; the new entry point's extra hypothesis hA is flagged and discharged by Phase 3.
dead_ends: Marin-Morales-Strassburger labIK-le: base is IK not CK, settles IS5 not CS5. Not planned.
Any route needing box(A or B) -> (box A or box B): not a theorem of classical S5. No phase attempts it.
Relabeling retractions: every one is forced to identify the two tag copies. Bound landed as an asset only.
Product model over IS5: closed by the R-b/collapse equivalence.
